Goals.title: Goals
Goals.disclaimer: This is an estimate based on standard formulas, not personalised medical advice.
Goals.medicalDisclaimer: This is not medical or dietetic advice. These numbers are a general estimate based on population-average formulas, not a personalised assessment of your body, health, or medical history. They don't account for medical conditions, medications, body composition, or other individual factors that can meaningfully change your real needs. For guidance tailored to you, consult a registered dietitian, doctor, or other qualified professional. Treat these numbers as a starting point — track your actual results over a few weeks and adjust as needed, rather than following them rigidly. Use at your own discretion.
Goals.explainCalories: We estimate your resting metabolic rate using the Mifflin-St Jeor equation, a widely used formula based on your height, weight, age, and sex. We then multiply it by an activity factor based on how active you told us you are, and adjust up or down depending on whether your goal is to lose, maintain, or gain weight.
Goals.explainProtein: Protein targets are based on published nutrition research recommending higher protein intake per kilogram of body weight for people who are more physically active, with a small additional allowance if your goal is to build muscle.
Goals.explainFatCarbs: Fat is set at roughly a quarter of your total calories. Carbs make up whatever calories are left once protein and fat are accounted for.
Goals.explainFibre: A general daily fibre target, not personalised to your other numbers.
Goals.explainWhy: These formulas are based on averages across large groups of people. Your actual needs depend on things they can't measure — body composition, genetics, health conditions, and more. Two people with identical height, weight, and age can have genuinely different real-world energy needs. Use these numbers as an informed starting point, not a guarantee.

About.title: About Macro Tracker
About.intro: I built this app for anyone who, like me, finds it hard to stay on top of what they're eating — the idea is simple: paying close attention to exactly what goes into your body makes it much easier to actually reach your goals, whatever they are. Whether you're looking to lose weight, build muscle, or just maintain where you're at, this app is built to support that.
About.goalsText1: You can enter your own daily calorie and macro targets directly, or let the app estimate them for you based on your height, weight, age, sex, activity level, and goal. This calculator uses standard, widely-used nutrition formulas — but it's still just an estimate.
About.goalsDisclaimer: It is not medical or dietetic advice
About.goalsText2: , and it doesn't know anything about your individual health, body composition, or medical history. Treat it as a sensible starting point, track how your body actually responds over a few weeks, and adjust from there. For guidance tailored specifically to you, speak to a doctor or registered dietitian.
About.databaseText1: Add the foods you eat regularly, along with their nutritional values per 100g. To make this faster, you can:
About.databaseSearch: Search a nutrition database for generic foods, powered by the USDA FoodData Central database
About.databaseBarcode: Scan a barcode on packaged food, using data from Open Food Facts
About.databaseText2: Both of these pull from large, independent, third-party databases — genuinely useful, but not infallible. Occasionally an entry may be incomplete, outdated, or simply wrong.
About.databaseDisclaimer: I'd recommend double-checking any values against the actual packaging before relying on them
About.databaseText3: , especially for anything where accuracy really matters to you. I take no responsibility for inaccurate data provided by USDA or Open Food Facts.
About.loggingText: Once your food database is set up, logging is simple: weigh what you eat, log it, and the app tracks your calories and macros for the day against your goals. A few things that make this faster day to day:
About.loggingCopy: Copy entries from a previous day, so you're not re-logging the same breakfast every morning
About.loggingShare: Share access with someone else — a partner, family member, or friend — so you can each add to one another's food database and daily log
About.progressText: The History page lets you look back at any previous day to see what you ate and how it compared to your goals — useful for spotting patterns and tracking progress over time.
About.closing: I hope you find this useful. If you run into any problems or have suggestions, I'd genuinely like to hear them — reach me at
About.recipesText: You can also combine ingredients into a recipe — a meal you cook regularly, for example — and the app will automatically calculate its total nutrition per 100g. Once created, a recipe appears in your food database just like any other food, ready to log.
About.installHeading: Installing this app on your phone
About.installText: You can add Macro Tracker to your home screen so it opens like a regular app, with its own icon and no browser bar.
About.installAndroidText: Open the site in Chrome, tap the ⋮ menu in the top right, and choose "Add to Home screen" or "Install app".
About.installIosText: This only works in Safari — not Chrome, Ecosia, or other browsers. Open the site in Safari, tap the Share icon, scroll down, and choose "Add to Home Screen".
